transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because my head just hasn’t been clear lately, especially at work. I’ll be sitting with a client and suddenly realize I’ve lost the thread of what they were saying, and then I feel awful because, you know, I’m supposed to be paying attention.

And even chart notes—stuff I normally can do—I keep rereading the same line over and over like it’s not going in. Then I get stuck on simple decisions I used to just handle. It’s been making work feel… harder than it should.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

I don’t know… “sad” feels like a big word. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m kind of low, I guess, but then I start thinking maybe I’m just tired or stressed. It’s hard to separate it out.

Like yesterday, I was making coffee and just stood there staring at the mug for a while, which sounds ridiculous, and then I remembered this client I had who used to do the exact same thing—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I’m not totally sure how to answer.
Have you been enjoying things you typically find pleasurable?

Not really, no. Like… my guitar’s just been sitting in the corner, and I keep looking at it like I should pick it up, but then I don’t.

I’ve also been bailing on soccer, and I used to like going to the shelter too, but I keep not showing up. Even stuff like cooking or going hiking—things I normally enjoy—it’s like I’m doing the steps, but there’s no point to it. It just feels kind of empty.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

Um… anxious? I’m not sure. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m walking around panicking or anything.

Sometimes I feel kind of wound up, but then I wonder if that’s just normal, like when my schedule gets messed up. I had this one supervisor in school who used to say everyone calls everything anxiety now—sorry, that’s probably not helpful.

I guess I haven’t really noticed being especially on edge. Not in a clear way, anyway.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight lately?

Yeah… I think so. I haven’t really been weighing myself or anything, but my pants have been fitting looser, which I noticed because I kept having to pull them up at work, and then I was thinking maybe I just stretched them out or washed them wrong—sorry.

I guess I haven’t been eating much. Most days I don’t really feel hungry until someone says something like, “Did you eat?” and then I realize I skipped a meal without meaning to.
Do you feel like you're still able to experience pleasure when you do engage in those activities, even if it's just going through the motions?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of the thing. Even when I do make myself do it, it doesn’t really land the way it used to.

Like with cooking, I’ll chop stuff and follow the recipe, and normally I’d be tasting it and messing with it, but lately it’s just… steps. Same with hiking, I’m technically outside and moving, but I’m mostly just waiting for it to be over, which feels weird because I used to actually like it.

And the guitar—I keep thinking if I pick it up maybe it’ll click, but most of the time it just stays there. Soccer and the shelter too, I keep bailing before I even get to the part where I’d know if I enjoyed it. It all just feels kind of pointless, I guess.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… I think about a month? It kind of started after the clinic lost some staff and my schedule got shifted around.

I got put on more late-evening coverage, and there’s been a lot more crisis paperwork, which is… I mean, paperwork is always bad, but this has been heavier. At first I thought I was just tired from the schedule change, like anyone would be, but it hasn’t really lifted. So yeah, roughly a month.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Yeah… a lot, actually. Mostly about work.

Like if I miss one little detail in a note, or I forget to call someone back right away, I just start telling myself I’m useless. Like I’m letting the clients down, and everyone at the clinic down too. Which—sometimes it’s not even a huge thing, you know? Like it’s something I can fix, or someone else probably wouldn’t think twice about it.

But I’ll keep replaying it. I’ll be at home thinking about a note, or whether I sounded distracted on the phone, and then it turns into this whole thing in my head about how maybe I’m just bad at this and people are counting on me and I’m failing them. It’s kind of… constant lately.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like you're speeding up in your actions lately?

I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed anything obvious like… pacing around or talking really fast, if that’s what you mean.

Moving slowly—maybe? But it’s hard to tell because at work everything kind of feels slow when I’m buried in forms, and then at home I can sit there for too long before doing something. But I don’t know if other people would notice it. My roommate hasn’t said anything. 

Sorry, I’m kind of answering around it. I guess I haven’t clearly noticed myself being sped up or slowed down in a physical way.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself lately?

Um… yeah, kind of. Not like—I don’t have a plan or anything to hurt myself.

It’s more these thoughts that show up, usually when I’m really worn out, like… it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And then I feel scared for even thinking that, because I know that’s not nothing. I’ve had clients say things like that, and I know what it can mean, so it’s… yeah. It scares me.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still lately?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed.

I mean, I do bounce my leg sometimes, but I’ve kind of always done that, like in class or when I’m sitting through a long meeting. My history teacher used to call me out for it, which is funny because then I’d just get more aware of it and do it more. But lately… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I can’t sit still or anything.

I guess if I’m uncomfortable I shift around, but I haven’t noticed anything big.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past month?

I haven’t weighed myself, so I don’t know the exact number. But… yeah, my pants have been getting looser, and I’ve realized I’m skipping meals without really meaning to.

Most days I don’t even feel hungry until someone says something, like asks if I’ve eaten. Which is weird because I used to be pretty routine about lunch. At work I’ll just get caught up in paperwork or whatever, and then suddenly it’s late and I’m like, oh, I didn’t eat. So… maybe not a “significant amount” that I can measure, but I think I’ve lost some weight.
Have you noticed any significant changes in how quickly or slowly you're moving compared to your normal pace?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself moving slower or faster in a really obvious way.

Like, sometimes people talk about it as if it’s super visible, and I keep thinking of this guy in one of my classes who would always walk like he was late to something, even when he wasn’t—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. For me… I mean, I’m probably not paying close attention. I get through what I need to do, maybe a little more slowly if I’m tired, but I don’t know if that’s a change in my movement exactly.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve noticed a significant change.
Have you been feeling worthless or like you're not a good person?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I sit there thinking I’m a terrible person all day, but if I mess up even one small thing at the clinic—like miss a detail in a note, or don’t return a call right away—I just start telling myself I’m useless.

And it kind of spirals. Like, I’ll think I’m letting the clients down, and then the staff, and then everyone is probably having to deal with me not doing things right. Which… I know, objectively, people miss things sometimes. I’ve seen other people do it and I’d never judge them that harshly. But when it’s me, it feels different. Like it says something bad about me.
Do you feel like you're a burden to others?

Yeah… I guess I do. Especially at the clinic.

Like if I miss one small detail in a note or forget to return a call right away, it’s not just, “Oh, I made a mistake.” I start thinking I’m useless, like everyone else has to pick up after me. And then I picture the clients being let down, and the staff having to deal with whatever I didn’t do right.

It’s probably not even as big as it feels, but in my head it turns into this whole thing where I’m just… making things harder for everyone.
Do you think others have noticed any changes in how quickly or slowly you're moving?

I don’t think so… nobody’s said anything to me about it, at least.

I mean, sometimes I wonder if people at the clinic notice more than they say, because everyone’s kind of busy but also weirdly observant, you know? Like there’s always someone noticing if the copier is jammed or if the coffee’s out, which isn’t the same thing at all, sorry.

But no—no one has pointed out that I’m moving slower or faster or anything. If they have noticed, they haven’t told me.
How long have you been feeling worthless or like you're not a good person?

Probably about a month now. It sort of started after the clinic lost some staff and my schedule got moved into more late-evening coverage, and there’s been more crisis paperwork too.

I mean, I don’t know if it was like one specific day where I woke up and felt that way, but around then it started creeping in more. The whole place felt kind of stretched thin, and then I’d miss something small and it would just… land harder than it used to.
Have you caught yourself doing repetitive movements, like hand wringing or pacing back and forth, when you're feeling anxious or overwhelmed?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t think I do hand wringing, not that I’ve noticed.

Pacing, maybe? But I also pace when I’m trying to remember where I put something, or when the printer at the clinic decides to make that awful grinding noise and everyone pretends they don’t hear it. So I don’t know if that counts as anxiety or just… being at work.

I haven’t had anyone point it out to me, though. I guess I’m not always paying attention to what my hands or feet are doing when I’m overwhelmed.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that others can't?

No… I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t see.

I mean, sometimes if I’m really tired I’ll think I heard my name at work, but then it’s usually just someone talking down the hall or the phones doing that weird half-ring thing. The clinic has this one hallway where sound carries strangely, so you think someone’s right behind you and they’re actually by the front desk.

But no, nothing like… voices talking to me or seeing things that aren’t there. At least not that I’ve noticed.
